analytical_models.equation_role: Fit of simulated unit-cell volumes to obtain the bulk modulus B0
νl[100] = sqrt(C11/ρ); νt[100] = sqrt(C44/ρ); νl[111] = sqrt((C11 + 2 C12 + 4 C44)/(3ρ)) — used to determine C11, C44 and C12
Volume-conserving orthorhombic distortion E(δ) = E(0) + (C11 − C12) V δ² + O(δ⁴) gives C11 and C12; monoclinic distortion E(δ) = E(0) + ½ C44 V δ² + O(δ⁴) gives C44
analytical_models.model_note: For the tetragonal crystal structure three additional independent constants C13, C33 and C66 are determined using the scheme of ref. 40.
Used to derive the bulk modulus, anisotropy factor, shear modulus and Young's modulus along [100] and [111].

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Structure optimization: Brillouin-zone integration with an 18 × 18 × 18 Monkhorst-Pack grid; real-space grid with 50 Ryd energy cut-off; augmentation charges expanded to 600 Ryd; a 30 × 30 × 30 grid with 60 Ryd energy cut-off used for electronic density of states and formation-energy calculations; bulk modulus from simulated unit-cell volumes fitted with a Murnaghan equation of state; dynamical matrices from the linear response of the electronic subsystem in the harmonic approximation; DOS by the tetrahedron method on a 30 × 30 × 30 mesh.
computational_details.potential_model_or_database: Generalized gradient approximation (GGA) of Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof (PBE), spin-polarized; ultrasoft pseudo-potentials created on a modified Rappe-Rabe-Kaxiras-Joannopoulos (RRKJ) scheme
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: The calculated lattice parameter of ordered FeAl-B2 (with and without spin effects) was slightly less than the experimental value but in good agreement; calculated lattice constants for Fe3AlC-L1'2 and Mn-substituted κ-carbides agreed with reported experimental data (Fig. 6).

interfaces.interface_notes: The paper notes in general that the characteristics of ordered phases are determined by their degree of coherency with the matrix, but no specific coherency value is reported for this sample.
interfaces.phase_evolution: At annealing temperatures of 900–1050 °C, B2 forms as micron-sized particles (2–4 μm) and grain-boundary precipitates in the austenite (γ) phase and as nano-sized disc-like precipitates in the ferrite (α) phase; in the Ni-containing sample the B2 is of NiAl type. Coarse B2 particles in γ have a lower Ni content (and higher Al content) than the nano-sized disc-like B2 in α, and the nano-discs are the hardest feature.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: α + B2 composite nano-hardness at 1050 °C: 13.5 GPa for the Ni-containing alloy vs 8.3 GPa for the Ni-free alloy
γ + B2 composite nano-hardness at 1050 °C: 8.2 GPa for the Ni-containing alloy vs 7 GPa for the Ni-free alloy

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Two duplex lightweight steels Fe-15Mn-10Al-0.8C-5Ni and Fe-15Mn-10Al-0.8C were melted in an induction furnace (applies to both grades).

Highest annealing temperature, selected to study the change in nanomechanical properties arising from an increase in the Ni and Al content of the nano-sized disc-like B2 particles. Holding time not reported.

structures.overall_structure: Duplex γ + α matrix. B2 is present as coarse micron-sized particles and grain-boundary precipitates in the austenite (γ) phase and as nano-sized disc-like precipitates in the ferrite (α) phase; in the Ni-containing sample this B2 is of NiAl type. At 1050 °C the γ phase no longer contains stable nano-sized cuboid κ.

unmapped_findings: The Ni-containing alloy is labelled Fe-15Mn-10Al-0.8C-5Ni in the abstract, introduction, materials and results text, but Tables 1 and 2 label the same alloy as Fe-15Mn-10Al-0.5C-5Ni (0.5C); this appears to be a typographical inconsistency in the carbon content.

For the 1050 °C Ni-containing sample the α + B2 composite gave the highest measured hardness (13.5 GPa), which Table 2 identifies as the hardest composite measured; the increase in hardness is attributed to the NiAl-type B2 discs in α (Ni-Al bonds stronger than Fe-Al bonds).
Conclusions state that in the Ni-containing alloys annealed at 900–1050 °C the ferritic phase produced a hard structure of about 10 GPa due to the dispersion of nano-sized discs of B2 phase.

According to the Orowan mechanism the increase in shear stress Δτ is proportional to the inverse of the precipitate diameter (Δτ ∝ R^−1.25), so the higher hardness values at higher annealing temperatures are also attributed to the uniformly distributed nano-sized disc-like B2 particles increasing the shear resistance of the α matrix.

The DFT calculations of this study were performed on the ordered compounds FeAl-B2, Fe3Al-L12, Fe3AlC-L1'2, Fe2MnAlC, FeMn2AlC and Mn3AlC (κ-carbides) to obtain elastic constants and Young's moduli; NiAl-type B2 was not computed by DFT, so the ab-initio results principally underpin the κ-phase and the Ni-free B2 behaviour rather than the Ni-containing 1050 °C state.
